option_description: Attestation that the log/telemetry channel from source to collector/SIEM is wrapped in TLS end-to-end (e.g. syslog-over-TLS on 6514 per RFC 5425, or OTLP with a configured tls block).
security_impact: Sole OR-trigger of "Cleartext log transport (sniffing and disclosure)" — fires when flow_tls_encrypted is false, mapping to ATT&CK T1040. Also supporting context for "MITM modification of events in transit" (RFC 5425 §5 disclosure/modification threats; NIST SP 800-92 §4.5 mandates protection of audit information in transit; PCI DSS Req 10 / Req 4 require encryption of audit transport).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe the collector's syslog/OTLP ingest port with openssl s_client to confirm a TLS handshake completes and that cleartext on the same port is refused.
how_to_obtain.command: openssl s_client -connect <collector_host>:6514 -showcerts </dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Successful TLS handshake on the syslog/OTLP ingest port; cleartext connect to the same host:port should fail or be refused.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Sweep the canonical syslog/OTLP ports to confirm plaintext variants are closed and only TLS-wrapped ingress answers.
how_to_obtain.command: nmap -p 514,601,6514,4317,4318 --script ssl-enum-ciphers <collector_host>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Plaintext syslog ports (514 UDP/TCP, 601) closed; only TLS-wrapped ingress (6514 syslog-TLS, 4317/4318 OTLP w/ TLS) is open and answers a TLS handshake.
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 5425 + OpenTelemetry Collector security config best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep the OpenTelemetry Collector config for tls blocks on every receiver and exporter that crosses a trust boundary.
how_to_obtain.command: yq '.receivers.*.protocols.*.tls' otelcol-config.yaml; yq '.exporters.*.tls' otelcol-config.yaml
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Every receiver and exporter that crosses a trust boundary has a tls: block with cert_file/key_file/ca_file set; no exporter sets insecure: true in production.
how_to_obtain.source: OpenTelemetry Collector — Security Configuration Best Practices

option_description: TLS floor on the log flow — the lowest protocol version the forwarder/collector/SIEM endpoints will negotiate.
security_impact: Contextual evidence for "MITM modification of events in transit" — not its load-bearing OR-trigger, but a weak floor (TLS 1.0/1.1/SSLv3 accepted) widens the cert/integrity gap and enables downgrade-then-rewrite. RFC 5425 mandates TLS 1.2 support; NIST SP 800-52r2 bars TLS <1.2 for federal use.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate the protocols offered by the collector's TLS ingest with testssl.sh.
how_to_obtain.command: testssl.sh --protocols <collector_host>:6514
how_to_obtain.expected_output: TLSv1.2 and/or TLSv1.3 offered; TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, SSLv3 are 'not offered' (good).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the min_version field on every Collector receiver/exporter tls block.
how_to_obtain.command: yq '.receivers.*.protocols.*.tls.min_version, .exporters.*.tls.min_version' otelcol-config.yaml
how_to_obtain.expected_output: min_version: "1.2" or "1.3" set explicitly on every receiver/exporter tls block (per configtls README).

option_description: Attestation that forwarders validate the collector's certificate chain AND hostname end-to-end — no insecure_skip_verify, no insecure: true, no pinning to a self-signed cert without verification.
security_impact: One OR-trigger of "MITM modification of events in transit" — fires when server_certificate_validated is false, mapping to ATT&CK T1565.002 (Transmitted Data Manipulation) and T1557 (AiTM). RFC 5425 §5 names modification as a primary syslog-transport threat; OWASP ASVS V7 requires authenticated transport for audit data.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep the OpenTelemetry exporter tls blocks for the verification-disabling fields and confirm a real CA bundle is pinned.
how_to_obtain.command: yq '.exporters.*.tls.insecure, .exporters.*.tls.insecure_skip_verify, .exporters.*.tls.ca_file, .exporters.*.tls.server_name_override' otelcol-config.yaml
how_to_obtain.expected_output: insecure: false (or absent), insecure_skip_verify: false (or absent), ca_file points to a real trust bundle.
how_to_obtain.source: OpenTelemetry Collector — Security Configuration Best Practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interpose a MITM proxy with an untrusted cert between forwarder and collector and observe the forwarder's behaviour.
how_to_obtain.command: Stand up a MITM proxy with an untrusted cert between forwarder and collector and observe the forwarder's behavior.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Forwarder refuses to send (cert validation failure logged); does NOT silently deliver to the proxy.

option_description: Attestation that events crossing this flow carry per-event or per-batch integrity protection (HMAC, signed envelope, hash-chained batch, or equivalent) and the SIEM verifies it.
security_impact: One OR-trigger of "MITM modification of events in transit" — fires when log_pipeline_integrity_protected is false, mapping to ATT&CK T1565.002. NIST AU-9 explicitly requires audit information be protected from unauthorized modification (defence-in-depth beyond TLS, so a stripped/terminated session cannot silently rewrite events).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the pipeline design: is each event (or batch) signed/HMAC'd at the source, and is the chain verified at the SIEM?
how_to_obtain.command: Review the pipeline design: is each event (or batch) signed/HMAC'd at the source, and is the chain verified at the SIEM?
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented integrity mechanism (e.g. signed envelopes, hash-chained batches, blockchain notarisation) with a periodic verification job.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-92 + NIST AU-9 (Protection of Audit Information)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inject a synthetic event into the queue/wire and confirm the SIEM rejects or flags it on the integrity check.
how_to_obtain.command: Inject a synthetic event into the queue/wire and confirm the SIEM rejects or flags it on integrity check.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Injected event flagged as unsigned/unauthenticated; alert raised.

option_description: Attestation that the log-forwarder-to-collector channel enforces mutual TLS — both peers present and validate X.509 certificates per RFC 5425 §4.2.
security_impact: One OR-trigger of "Forwarder masquerade / spoofed log source" — fires when service_to_service_mtls_enforced is false, mapping to ATT&CK T1565.001 (Stored Data Manipulation via spoofed events). RFC 5425 §4.2 makes certificate-based authentication of both peers a MUST; OWASP ASVS V7 names non-repudiation of log sources as a core requirement.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt a TLS handshake to the collector without presenting a client cert and confirm it is rejected.
how_to_obtain.command: openssl s_client -connect <collector_host>:6514 -showcerts </dev/null  # without a client cert
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Handshake fails / certificate_required alert when no client cert is presented (collector requires mTLS).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm every external-facing Collector receiver has client_ca_file set and require_client_certificate: true.
how_to_obtain.command: yq '.receivers.*.protocols.*.tls.client_ca_file, .receivers.*.protocols.*.tls.require_client_certificate' otelcol-config.yaml
how_to_obtain.expected_output: client_ca_file is set AND require_client_certificate: true on every external-facing receiver.

option_description: Attestation that each emitting workload presents its own cryptographic identity (SPIFFE SVID, per-pod client cert, or unique API key) — not a shared cluster-wide secret.
security_impact: One OR-trigger of "Forwarder masquerade / spoofed log source" — fires when identity_propagated_cryptographically is false, mapping to ATT&CK T1565.001. A shared/static credential destroys non-repudiation (OWASP ASVS V7) — a compromised pod can impersonate any other workload's logs at the SIEM.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review forwarder bootstrap and inventory the distinct identities seen at the collector over a 24h window, mapping each back to one workload.
how_to_obtain.command: Review forwarder bootstrap: list distinct client certs / SPIFFE SVIDs / API keys seen at the collector over a 24h window and map each back to one workload.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Distinct identity per workload (1:1 mapping); no single credential observed from more than one source workload/host.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP ASVS V7 (logging non-repudiation) + OpenTelemetry security best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the collector access log for client_cert_subject or auth_principal and group by source IP/pod.
how_to_obtain.command: Query collector access log for client_cert_subject or auth_principal; group by source IP/pod.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: One auth_principal per source; no broadcast principal like 'logger' or 'fluentd-shared'.

option_description: Attestation that the forwarder/source masks or redacts secrets (API tokens, passwords, JWTs, session identifiers, private-key material) BEFORE events enter the pipeline — not at the central SIEM after exposure.
security_impact: One OR-trigger of "Secrets and PII leakage into log bodies (CWE-532)" — fires when secrets_masked_in_logs is false, mapping to ATT&CK T1552.001 (Credentials In Files). CWE-532 (Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File), OWASP ASVS V7, and OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet all forbid credentials in logs; PCI DSS Req 10 forbids storing authentication data in audit logs.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a redaction processor is wired into the Collector pipeline with explicit blocked_values regex covering token/secret patterns.
how_to_obtain.command: yq '.processors.redaction' otelcol-config.yaml   # or fluentd/vector equivalent
how_to_obtain.expected_output: redaction processor wired with allow_all_keys: false, blocked_values covering card/token/secret patterns (e.g. '4[0-9]{12}', 'Bearer [A-Za-z0-9_-]+').
how_to_obtain.source: OpenTelemetry redaction processor + CWE-532 + OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Sample recent events in the SIEM and grep for known credential patterns; any hit is a P0 incident.
how_to_obtain.command: Sample 10k recent events in the SIEM and grep for regex patterns: PAN, JWT, 'password=', private-key headers.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Zero hits; any hit is a P0 incident and triggers the redaction-failure runbook.

option_description: Attestation that personally identifiable information and regulated data (PAN/card numbers, government IDs, full email/phone where not required, health identifiers) are excluded or tokenized at the source before they enter the log pipeline.
security_impact: One OR-trigger of "Secrets and PII leakage into log bodies (CWE-532)" — fires when pii_excluded_from_logs is false, mapping to ATT&CK T1552.001. CWE-532 explicitly forbids sensitive data in logs; OWASP ASVS V7 requires no PAN/payment data in logs; PCI DSS Req 10 forbids storing cardholder data in audit trails.

how_to_obtain.instruction: SIEM-grep recent events for PAN and national-ID regex patterns to confirm zero hits.
how_to_obtain.command: Sample 10k recent events in the SIEM and grep for regex patterns: PAN, JWT, 'password=', private-key headers.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Zero hits; any hit is a P0 incident and triggers the redaction-failure runbook.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the redaction processor's blocked_values include the PII patterns specific to the data domain (PAN, national ID, etc.).
how_to_obtain.command: yq '.processors.redaction' otelcol-config.yaml
how_to_obtain.expected_output: blocked_values regex covers PAN (e.g. '4[0-9]{12}'), national-ID patterns, and any domain-specific PII; allow_all_keys: false.
how_to_obtain.source: OpenTelemetry redaction processor + CWE-532 + OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet

option_description: Attestation that the log archive / SIEM destination is tamper-evident — WORM, S3 Object Lock (Compliance/Governance), Azure Immutable Blob, GCS Bucket Lock, or append-only indices.
security_impact: Sole OR-trigger of "Indicator removal at destination — mutable log archive" — fires when audit_log_tamper_evident is false, mapping to ATT&CK T1070 (Indicator Removal). NIST AU-9 requires audit information be protected from unauthorized modification/deletion; PCI DSS Req 10.5 requires audit-trail integrity at rest.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the archive bucket's Object Lock configuration to confirm immutability is enabled with a retention period.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-object-lock-configuration --bucket <log-archive-bucket>   # or equivalent in Azure Immutable Blob / GCS Bucket Lock
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ObjectLockEnabled: Enabled with Compliance or Governance mode and a retention period set.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST AU-9 + MITRE ATT&CK T1070 (Indicator Removal on Host)

how_to_obtain.instruction: As a privileged operator, attempt to delete a recent archived log object and confirm the deletion is denied and itself logged.
how_to_obtain.command: Attempt to delete a recent archived log object as a privileged operator.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Delete is denied by Object Lock / immutability policy; attempt is itself logged.

option_description: Attestation that a dead-man-switch fires when a source falls silent or the ingest pipeline drops — heartbeat-missing / source-silent-> N min / ingest-rate-collapse rules per critical source class with a documented SLO.
security_impact: Sole OR-trigger of "Silent collection failure — no dead-man-switch alarm" — fires when logging_failure_alerting_enabled is false, mapping to ATT&CK T1562.006 (Indicator Blocking). NIST AU-5 explicitly requires response to audit-processing failures; OWASP ASVS V7 requires alerting when logging stops.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect SIEM detection rules for heartbeat-missing / source-silent / ingest-rate-collapse alerts per critical source class.
how_to_obtain.command: Inspect SIEM detection rules for 'heartbeat missing' / 'source silent > N minutes' / 'ingest rate dropped > X%'.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Dead-man-switch rules exist per critical source class with a defined SLO (e.g. silence > 15 min => page).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Drill: stop a non-prod log forwarder and measure time-to-page against the documented SLO.
how_to_obtain.command: Stop a non-prod log forwarder and time how long until the on-call is paged.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Page within the documented SLO (e.g. <= 15 min); not 'we noticed the next day'.

option_description: Attestation that every log source keeps its clock synchronized to a trusted time source (NTP/Chrony, stratum <=4) within bounded skew (e.g. < 1s RMS offset).
security_impact: One OR-trigger of "Backdated / clock-skewed events break correlation" — fires when clocks_synced_to_trusted_time_source is false, mapping to ATT&CK T1070.006 (Timestomp-adjacent). NIST SP 800-92 §4.4 mandates time synchronization across log sources so cross-source correlation holds.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On every log source, query chrony/ntp for synchronization status, stratum, and offset.
how_to_obtain.command: chronyc tracking   # or: timedatectl status; ntpq -p
how_to_obtain.expected_output: System clock synchronized: yes; Last offset / RMS offset < 1 second; Stratum <=4.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Plot the distribution of (event_received_at - event_timestamp) per source in the SIEM and alert on outliers.
how_to_obtain.command: In the SIEM, plot the distribution of (event_received_at - event_timestamp) per source; alert on outliers.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Skew per source within +/- 1s; no source emitting non-UTC timestamps.

option_description: Attestation that all sources emit event timestamps in UTC with sub-second resolution (not local timezone, not a zone-naive wall clock).
security_impact: One OR-trigger of "Backdated / clock-skewed events break correlation" — fires when timestamps_in_utc is false, mapping to ATT&CK T1070.006. NIST SP 800-92 and OWASP ASVS V7 require unambiguous timestamps so cross-source correlation works and no timezone-shift evasion window exists.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Sample raw events at the collector and confirm they carry RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 UTC timestamps with sub-second precision.
how_to_obtain.command: In the SIEM, plot the distribution of (event_received_at - event_timestamp) per source; alert on outliers.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Skew per source within +/- 1s; no source emitting non-UTC timestamps.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the logging schema/contract (JSON schema, OTel semantic conventions) for an explicit UTC timestamp field.
how_to_obtain.command: Inspect logging schema/contract (JSON schema, OTel semantic conventions) covering these required fields.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented schema enforcing required-field set including timestamp_utc with sub-second precision; CI gate rejects schema-violating events.

option_description: Attestation that the log/telemetry pipeline enforces per-source rate limits AND bounded queues / backpressure (OpenTelemetry memory_limiter, sending_queue, max_recv_msg_size_mib) so a noisy or compromised source cannot exhaust the SIEM.
security_impact: Sole OR-trigger of "Telemetry flood — DoS of SIEM ingest" — fires when log_flood_overflow_protection is false, mapping to ATT&CK T1499.003 (Application Exhaustion Flood). Doubles as evasion cover: a flood from one source can drown another's signal. NIST SP 800-92 calls out volume management as a logging-infrastructure design concern.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep the Collector config for memory_limiter, sending_queue size, and per-receiver max message size caps.
how_to_obtain.command: yq '.processors.memory_limiter, .exporters.*.sending_queue, .receivers.*.protocols.*.max_recv_msg_size_mib' otelcol-config.yaml
how_to_obtain.expected_output: memory_limiter configured (check_interval, limit_mib); sending_queue.queue_size bounded; max recv message size capped.
how_to_obtain.source: OpenTelemetry Collector — Security Configuration Best Practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Plot per-source EPS in the SIEM over 30 days and confirm an alert fires on >3x baseline without dropping other sources' data.
how_to_obtain.command: Plot per-source EPS in the SIEM over 30 days; alert on >3x baseline.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Per-source rate cap exists; spikes trigger alert without dropping other sources' data.
